text:
raj: Following up on yesterday's RFC session  we didn't close the cohort vs per-tenant micro-lane decision. Putting notes here so we have a single source of truth.
maya: Thanks. Quick summary from my side: micro-lanes give isolation for p99-critical tenants, but cost us batching efficiency and KV locality. Cohorts are efficient but noisy neighbors are real.
liam: Practical constraint: GPUs prefer larger, steady batches. If we splinter into many tiny per-tenant lanes we blow throughput and increase per-token cost.
sophia: KV affinity is the killer here. When a tenant hops between lanes or the lane is too small, KV cold misses spike and p99 explodes. We shouldn't ignore that.
nana: (ana) Another lever: admission credit baseline + headroom multiplier. Instead of hard per-tenant queue, give small tenants a prioritized micro-lane with limited concurrency and credits so they keep low latency without starving bigger cohorts.
raj: Proposed topology: three lane classes — micro (per-tenant, SLA-tagged), mid cohorts (short/med seq_len buckets), and bulk (long seqs). Router picks lane by SLA then size hints.
maya: Config implications: each lane needs its own coalescing/window config, preemption policy, and kv-cache warming strategy. That's a lot of surface area.
liam: Implementation cost: we already have per-operator window hooks. Refactor needed: lane metadata must travel with requests into coalescer so it can apply per-lane windows. Not tiny but doable.
sophia: Observability must be lane-first: histograms labeled by lane and tenant, kv-hit-by-lane, batch-size distribution, and model-variant tags. Otherwise debugging cross-lane issues will be painful.
nana: Edge-case: bursty tenant that oscillates between mid-cohort and micro-lane. We should avoid flip-flopping. Proposal: hysteresis with time and volume thresholds (e.g., 20s + sustained QPS).
raj: Preemption rules: emergency lanes > micro-lanes > cohorts. In constrained mode, evict cohort work first. But for fairness we need fallback routes (compact model or increased timeout) for preempted requests.
maya: Fallbacks must be route-configurable. Example rule: "on-preempt -> try compact-a1 for up to 50ms extra, else queue in best-effort cohort." Keep it declarative.
liam: Admission model idea: token-bucket per-tenant with a headroom multiplier based on recent latency SLAs. Credits consumed at enqueue time, replenished at steady rate, with emergency borrow allowed from a global pool.
sophia: That'd let small tenants burst briefly while protecting p99 of critical tenants. We should simulate different settings.
raj: Simulation plan: use trace-replay with realistic tenant mix (30% small, 10% SLA-critical, 60% mid/bulk). Inject KV cold-start events and a 3x global load spike. Collect tail latency and batch sizes.
nana: I can wire a sim that tags tenants and flips KV-hit flags. sim-bot: I will ingest traces and run with multiple configs when you push them.
sophia: Telemetry matrix (high level): per-lane p50/p95/p99, per-tenant p99 (for SLA tenants), batch-size CDF per lane, kv-hit-rate per lane, schedule-eviction-counts, fallback-routing-counts, model-variant-usage.
maya: Operational note: defaults should hide complexity. Expose an "auto" tuning mode that adjusts cohort boundaries and windows to meet p95/p99 targets for a tenant class. Manual overrides available for deploy teams.
raj: Open engineering tasks: (1) Router changes to emit lane labels, (2) Coalescer refactor to accept lane-specific window config, (3) Admission-credit service, (4) Observability labels and dashboards, (5) Trace simulation harness extension.
liam: I'll take (2) and (3) spike. Expect a small API sketch PR by EOD Friday.
sophia: I'll draft the observability dashboard and the auto-tune heuristic doc.
nana: I'll prototype the token-bucket + headroom numbers and post sim scripts.
maya: Let's not forget tests: regression test for KV cold-hit p99, oscillation test for cohort churn, and cost-per-token vs throughput benchmarks.
raj: Can someone add a short whiteboard snapshot and the spike scripts path here? maya: Uploaded whiteboard in thread. raj: Spike scripts added to infra/batching/spikes/hybrid-lane-sim.
liam: running a quick Local sim now; will post results.
sophia: Schedule: sync in 48 hours to review sim outputs and agree on the RFC update. @deploy-bot please create calendar invite 45m.
deploy-bot: Meeting created: "Hybrid batching lanes: sim review" on Mon 10:30 (invites: raj, maya, liam, sophia, ana).
raj: thanks. Any final concerns?
maya: One more: model-cache affinity when we change variant during fallback. Need to ensure model weights aren't thrashing between compact and full variants, or apply warm pools for compact variants.
liam: noted. I'll add model-variant warm pool as a potential mitigation.
sophia: I'll include that in the observability checklist. :mag:
nana: I'll post the prototype numbers and sim outputs here when ready.
raj: Great thread. Closing for now, will update RFC doc with decisions and remaining open items.
